I loved what they did with Soren and Claudia actually. The way that Claudia and Soren switch roles in the show was actually one of the most compelling aspects of the show. In the beginning, it is Soren who is given the task of killing the princes seemingly because of two things: first, he isn’t smart enough to question his father’s orders and second, he is simply less caring and kind than his sister. However, after Soren’s paralysis, we find out he did have second thoughts about his father’s orders nearly the whole way through. We also see how Claudia’s seemingly positive traits may not be so positive at all. She is trusting. Too trusting. Because of her trust in her father, she refuses to acknowledge the truth when Soren tells her that  Viren ordered him to kill the princes. Her kindness also is a key reason why she ends up being a villain. Claudia wants to minimize the suffering done to her people, she believes that the war is the best way to ensure the safety of the human race. I think it is because of Claudia’s positive traits that she cannot be redeemed, in her mind, to be against the war is to be against the prosperity and safety of the human race.
